correctness.rationale: Enumerating input digit pairs {0,1}^2 proves all four carry transitions with only 0/1 carries. Every n<4^k has no possible nonzero input above digit k, so the terminal zero-carry component equals the exact ordered-pair multiplicity. Two support states give a 2x2 transition matrix, characteristic polynomial t²−4t+2 and exact H_k formula. A double-coordinate Fibonacci induction bounds all 2^k digit outcomes, with explicit output words hitting F_{k+1}; monotone 4-adic bracketing proves both Theta exponents. The actual verify.py was executed successfully on 21,845 brute pairs and reachable states to depth21; infinite validity comes from proof, not test.

originality.rationale: The exact numeric H_k sequence is OEIS A007052 and is explicitly credited as known. Inspected full original Moser 1962 and De Bruijn 1964 papers and relevant OEIS records do not yield the same fixed coefficient-three positive sumset interpretation jointly with the sharp Fibonacci representation extremum. Literature and mathematical-record searches did not reveal stronger matching statements; full Eigen–Ito–Prasad 2004 text inaccessible and unindexed prior results remain possible.
residual_risks: Exact numerical H_k sequence is previously known (OEIS A007052); originality rests solely on its arithmetic meaning and independent sharp Fibonacci multiplicity theorem.
Earlier obscure or unindexed digit-carry literature may contain an equivalent coefficient-three result.
Full-text implications of Eigen–Ito–Prasad (2004) were not inspectable; abstract concerns signed rather than positive decompositions.
The 1962 print antecedent does not have a day-specific verified first-publication date; 2001-02-07 is the earliest verified day-stamped online public comment among the selected sources.

value.rationale: This treats the nearest nontrivial fixed-set coefficient perturbation of Moser's unique n=a+2b representation and completely determines both exact support counts and sharp extremal representation multiplicities for every power-of-four range. Distinct support and maximal-fiber exponents explain a natural simultaneous sparsity/overlap phenomenon. Not based on novel recurrence numbers alone; the structural carry model and Fibonacci maxima are motivated, precise and useful as additive benchmarks.
